title: TikTok Shop Seller Registration: Step-by-Step Guide for US Sellers
summary: Complete your TikTok Shop seller registration without errors. Learn required documents, Individual vs Business accounts, Seller Center setup, and probation rules.
body_markdown:
## The 'Zero-Rejection' Document Checklist and Verification Walkthrough


### Demystifying Required Documents: Passport, Driver's License, EIN, Business Licenses, and More


Documents requested depend on your account type and the fields shown during application. Individual sellers should have a current government-issued ID, such as a driver’s license or passport, available. Business applicants should prepare the entity’s legal registration details, an EIN when applicable, and identification for the authorized representative. An EIN supports business tax identification, but it does not replace company registration records or the representative’s identity document. Use the US **tiktok shop seller center** application prompts as the source of truth for the records required in your case.


**Document checklist:** Before opening the application, gather the ID requested for the applicant, entity records for a Business account, applicable EIN details, and any requested business license or registration document. Keep clear digital copies ready so you can submit the exact records requested.


### Formatting for Success: Photo Quality, Name Matching, and Address Accuracy


Upload a complete, readable image of each document. Avoid glare, shadows, cropped edges, blur, or edits that obscure details. Enter the applicant’s legal name exactly as it appears on the ID, including spelling and name order. For a Business account, match the entity name to its official record, and enter the authorized representative’s personal information in the fields intended for that person. Enter addresses consistently, including apartment or suite details when they appear in supporting records. Differences in spelling, abbreviations, or formatting can send an otherwise valid application for review.


### Common Verification Errors and How to Resolve Them (The Documentation Traps)


Frequent problems include submitting an expired or unreadable ID, entering a shop name instead of the legal entity name, and providing personal details where the form requests business information. An address mismatch can also interrupt verification. Read the rejection notice, identify the affected field, and correct that discrepancy before uploading a replacement. Use a record that directly supports the flagged field instead of submitting document types at random. Save copies of submitted documents and application details so you can track changes accurately.


### Desktop Seller Center vs. Mobile App: Navigating the Registration Interface Differences


The desktop US Seller Center portal and Seller Center mobile app provide seller tools, but their layouts and upload flows may differ. On desktop, a larger screen can make it easier to review fields, compare details with records, and check that uploaded files are legible. The app can be useful for completing tasks by phone, but confirm that each file is attached to the correct field. Whether you start through the portal or app, use the same legal information and follow your application prompts. The consumer-facing *tiktok shop app* is not the seller registration interface.


### Troubleshooting Failed Submissions: What to Do When Your Application Hits a Wall


If a submission fails, check for an in-app status message or a request for information. Compare the rejection reason against your ID, business record, and submitted fields, then replace only the inaccurate or unclear item. Keep screenshots or notes of the notice and correction. Use the support option in Seller Center if the reason remains unclear or the issue repeats. Support channels may begin with automated responses, so describe the problem precisely: name the document, affected field, and correction already attempted. Avoid creating a second application with conflicting details.
